item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"ChatGPT prompts to make writing sound human: 8 to copy","dek":"Eight copy and paste prompts, built on OpenAI's own prompting tips, that make ChatGPT write in your tone instead of its own, plus the settings that keep that style across chats.","summary":"Eight ChatGPT prompts that make drafts sound like a person: name the reader and tone, let ChatGPT learn your style from samples, rewrite stiff text and edit in steps. Custom Instructions, memory and project instructions keep the style in every new chat.","seo_title":"ChatGPT prompts to make writing sound human: 8 to copy","seo_description":"8 ChatGPT prompts to make writing sound human: set tone and reader, teach it your style from samples, fix stiff drafts, and save it in Custom Instructions.","answer_summary":"Tell ChatGPT who the reader is and name the tone in plain words, paste samples of your own writing and ask it to describe and then copy your style, and save that style in Custom Instructions under Personalize so every chat uses it.","tags":["ChatGPT","OpenAI","Prompts","Writing","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"ChatGPT prompts to make writing sound human work best when they tell the model exactly how you sound, not just that you want it to sound natural. OpenAI's own help page on prompting says ChatGPT responds better to clear, specific prompts with enough context, and suggests naming the tone you want with plain adjectives like formal, informal, friendly, professional, humorous or serious.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: Prompt engineering best practices for ChatGPT","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI's Academy page on customizing ChatGPT goes a step further. It says you can paste samples of your own writing, ask ChatGPT to describe your tone and style, and then ask it to mirror that style in a new draft. The prompts below are built on those two pages.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Academy: Customizing ChatGPT","url":"https://academy.openai.com/public/clubs/work-users-ynjqu/resources/customizing-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"One honest note first. No prompt makes ChatGPT write like you every time. It gets you closer, and the last ten percent is your own edit: read the draft out loud and cut every line you would never say.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Why ChatGPT writing sounds like ChatGPT","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"A vague request gets a generic answer. If you only say \"write an email to my landlord\", ChatGPT has to guess the reader, the mood and your voice, so it falls back on safe, polished, slightly stiff wording. Every detail you add removes one guess.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI's help page lists four techniques that matter here: give ChatGPT a role or persona, separate your text from your instructions with delimiters such as triple quotes, break the task into steps, and show examples of the result you want. It also recommends starting with a first prompt, reading the answer and refining the prompt instead of expecting a perfect draft on the first try.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: Prompt engineering best practices for ChatGPT","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"ChatGPT prompts to make writing sound human","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Name the reader and the tone","text":"Write a short email to [who], who [what they know or care about]. Tone: friendly and direct, like a coworker, not a press release. Use short sentences and plain words. Say what I need in the first line.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"This is the persona and tone advice from OpenAI's help page in one line. Naming the reader matters as much as naming the tone: a note to your manager and a note to a friend should not sound the same.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Let it learn your style","text":"Here are three things I wrote: \"\"\"[paste your writing]\"\"\" Summarize my tone and style, including word choice, sentence length and level of formality. Keep the summary to five bullet points.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"This comes almost word for word from OpenAI's Academy page, which suggests asking ChatGPT to summarize your tone and style from samples you paste. The triple quotes are the delimiter trick from the help page: they tell ChatGPT where your writing starts and stops.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: Prompt engineering best practices for ChatGPT","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt"},{"name":"OpenAI Academy: Customizing ChatGPT","url":"https://academy.openai.com/public/clubs/work-users-ynjqu/resources/customizing-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Write in that style","text":"Now write [the new piece] in my style, matching the tone, pacing and structure of my samples so it reads like I wrote it. Do not add phrases I never use.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Run this right after Prompt 2, in the same chat, so the style summary is still there. Paste real writing, like emails or messages you sent, not your most formal work, or you will get your most formal voice back.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Rewrite a stiff draft","text":"Rewrite the text in triple quotes so it sounds like a person talking. Keep every fact. Cut filler and buzzwords, use contractions, vary sentence length, and keep it as short as it can be. \"\"\"[paste draft]\"\"\"","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Tell ChatGPT what to keep, not only what to change. \"Keep every fact\" stops it from smoothing away the details that make the text yours.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Edit in steps","text":"You are given text in triple quotes. Step 1: list the sentences that sound robotic or overly formal. Step 2: explain in a few words why each one sounds that way. Step 3: rewrite only those sentences. \"\"\"[paste text]\"\"\"","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI's help page shows the same structure for editing: a prompt that asks ChatGPT to read the text, give feedback on grammar and structure, and then rewrite it with the edits. Splitting the work into steps lets you see what it changed and why, instead of getting a whole new text you have to check line by line.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: Prompt engineering best practices for ChatGPT","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Show one example","text":"Here is a message I like: \"\"\"[paste example]\"\"\" Write a new one about [topic] with the same length, tone and structure.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"This is what OpenAI calls one-shot prompting: a single example helps the model infer the pattern, style or type of response you expect. If one example is not enough, add two or three. That is few-shot prompting.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: Prompt engineering best practices for ChatGPT","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 7: Adjust for a different audience","text":"Recreate this style, but adjust it slightly for [a different audience, for example my boss instead of my team]. Keep it sounding like me.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI's Academy page gives a version of this prompt for the same voice aimed at a different audience, such as executives versus frontline staff.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Academy: Customizing ChatGPT","url":"https://academy.openai.com/public/clubs/work-users-ynjqu/resources/customizing-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 8: Ask for options, then pick","text":"Give me three versions of this opening line: one casual, one warm, one blunt. Keep each under 20 words.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Choosing between three short options is faster than fixing one long draft, and the version you pick tells ChatGPT more about your taste than any description.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Make the style stick across chats","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Put your style in Custom Instructions","text":"OpenAI's Academy page says Custom Instructions let you set preferences on tone, level of detail and areas of focus, and that you set them by going to your profile and clicking Personalize. Paste the five bullet style summary from Prompt 2 there, so every new chat starts with it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Turn on memory","text":"The same page suggests enabling memory so ChatGPT can remember your style preferences and reuse them across conversations, such as preferred formats, terminology or audiences.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Use project instructions for one kind of writing","text":"If you write in two voices, for example work updates and a personal blog, the Academy page says you can set project instructions that define the style and tone for a specific body of work. Make one project per voice.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Adjust in the chat for one-off changes","text":"For a single message that needs a different tone, just say so in the chat. The Academy page lists this as the third level of control, after your settings and your projects.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What these prompts will not do","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"They will not make ChatGPT know facts about your life, so check every detail it adds. They will not guarantee that a text passes an AI detector, and they are not a way to hand in work as your own where AI use is not allowed. What they do is cut the editing time between a generic draft and something you would actually send.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Keep your best prompts and your style summary in a note. Rebuilding them every time is where most of the time goes.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: The Freepik AI image generator is now Magnific. Here is how to use it
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Go to magnific.com and sign in with your Freepik email, Google or Apple login. Magnific says your subscription and remaining credits moved over. Freepik AI Image Generator is now Magnific Image Generator. Retouch became Magnific Image Editor. The Image Upscaler keeps its name. Images run on Nano Banana, Seedream, Flux and more. Video runs on Kling, Seedance, Veo and more. Sources: Magnific: Freepik AI is now Magnific, Magnific blog: From Freepik to Magnific, The Next Web, Tech.eu.

Freepik bought it in May 2024, according to Magnific's own timeline. Two years later the company put its whole AI stack under the Magnific name: image and video generation, editing, voice, an API and a canvas for teams.","sources":[{"name":"Magnific blog: From Freepik to Magnific","url":"https://www.magnific.com/blog/from-freepik-to-magnific-the-story-of-europes-largest-ai-creative-platform/"},{"name":"Magnific: Freepik AI is now Magnific","url":"https://www.magnific.com/freepik-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The business behind it is large. Tech.eu described the company as having more than 250 million creative assets in its library.","sources":[{"name":"The Next Web","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/freepik-rebrands-as-magnific"},{"name":"Tech.eu","url":"https://tech.eu/2026/04/28/freepik-rebrands-as-magnific-unifying-its-ai-creative-stack-as-enterprise-and-no-collar-growth-accelerates/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to log in to Magnific with your Freepik account","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Go to magnific.com","text":"Magnific says magnific.com is its only official website, and that other sites still using the Freepik AI name are not run by the company. If a page asks you to pay for \"Freepik AI\" somewhere else, close it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Sign in the way you always did","text":"Use the same email and password you used on Freepik, or the same Google or Apple sign in. You do not need a new account.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Check your plan and credits","text":"Magnific says your subscription and your remaining credits moved over from Freepik. If you paid for Freepik AI before the switch, that is what you should see after logging in.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Developers: Magnific says existing Freepik API keys work on Magnific, and the Freepik API is now the Magnific API. You do not need to rotate keys just because of the rename.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Old Freepik names and new Magnific names","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Most tools kept their job and changed their first word. Magnific lists the renames as: Freepik AI Image Generator to Magnific Image Generator, Freepik Retouch to Magnific Image Editor, Freepik Spaces to Magnific Spaces, Freepik Background Remover to Magnific Background Remover, Freepik AI Voice Generator to Magnific Voice Generator, and the Freepik app to the Magnific mobile app.","sources":[{"name":"Magnific: Freepik AI is now Magnific","url":"https://www.magnific.com/freepik-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Image Upscaler keeps its name, since it was the original Magnific product. One new piece arrived with the rebrand: Magnific inside ChatGPT and Claude, through MCP, so you can call its tools from a chat assistant.","sources":[{"name":"Magnific: Freepik AI is now Magnific","url":"https://www.magnific.com/freepik-ai"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Which models the Magnific Image Generator uses","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The image generator is not one model. Magnific says it runs Nano Banana, Seedream, Flux and more, and the video generator runs Kling, Seedance, Veo and more. The Next Web named Veo 3.1 and Seedance 2.0 among the video models you can select.","sources":[{"name":"Magnific: Freepik AI is now Magnific","url":"https://www.magnific.com/freepik-ai"},{"name":"The Next Web","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/freepik-rebrands-as-magnific"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Pick the model for the job instead of sticking with one. Run the same prompt on two image models and keep the better result. Each model has its own strengths, and they all sit in the same account, so comparing costs you a few minutes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Magnific's blog, the company also added Agents, MCP and Flows in June 2026, announced at its Upscale Conf in San Francisco, and launched a Business plan for smaller teams in January 2026.","sources":[{"name":"Magnific blog: From Freepik to Magnific","url":"https://www.magnific.com/blog/from-freepik-to-magnific-the-story-of-europes-largest-ai-creative-platform/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What this guide does not cover","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Magnific's documentation and pricing pages could not be checked for this guide, so it does not list credit costs, free plan limits or plan prices. Credit prices for AI tools change often. Check the pricing page inside your account before you start a big batch of images or videos, and compare what an image and a video cost before you queue either.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The honest summary: nothing you relied on in Freepik AI went away. The login, the credits and the API keys carry over. What changed is the name, the address and a longer list of models in one place. The main risk is the confusion itself, since lookalike sites can keep using the old Freepik AI name.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Bookmark magnific.com instead of searching for \"Freepik AI\" each time. It is the fastest way to avoid lookalike sites.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: InVideo AI for free: what you get before you pay
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: No card needed. You get 10 minutes of video generation and 4 exports every week, reset on Monday. Every free video carries a watermark. Generation, transcripts and paid stock cost credits. Editing and exports do not. A basic video model can cost 5 credits, a 4K Veo video over 100. Sources: InVideo Help Center: Can I use invideo AI for free, InVideo: AI credits and limits, InVideo: How do credits work, InVideo Help Center: Plans and credits, InVideo FAQ: Which plan is best for AI video creators, Creatify: InVideo AI review.

item.title: Google told schools no AI means no Search. Los Angeles just switched off AI Overviews anyway
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In early November, Google said K-12 student accounts would lose Gemini and Search unless school administrators turn them on. Its education chief told The New York Times that search and AI are deeply integrated. Los Angeles Unified has now blocked AI Overviews on school devices, part of its one year pause on student AI use. The district says Google did not play a role in the change. Google's headquarters in Mountain View, California. LAUSD's tech chief said the district could change its default search engine literally overnight. Sources: NBC Los Angeles, Los Angeles Magazine, LAist.

Because Google Search includes AI features by default, schools that keep AI off would lose Search as well, LAist reported.","sources":[{"name":"Los Angeles Magazine","url":"https://lamag.com/education/l-a-schools-block-googles-ai-overview-despite-companys-latest-ai-policy/"},{"name":"LAist","url":"https://laist.com/news/education/lausd-google-artificial-intelligence-search-gemini"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Chris Phillips, Google's vice president for education, told The New York Times that search and AI are deeply integrated, and that students at schools that ban AI would see a message saying Search is not available, according to both LAist and Los Angeles Magazine. Schools that opt in can use a Guided Learning mode meant to help students work through problems without skipping to the answer.","sources":[{"name":"Los Angeles Magazine","url":"https://lamag.com/education/l-a-schools-block-googles-ai-overview-despite-companys-latest-ai-policy/"},{"name":"LAist","url":"https://laist.com/news/education/lausd-google-artificial-intelligence-search-gemini"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google said it is giving schools more choices over AI access, not fewer, NBC Los Angeles reported. According to The New York Times, as cited by NBC, the company declined to offer a version of Search without AI chatbot features.","sources":[{"name":"NBC Los Angeles","url":"https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/lausd-disables-google-ai-overviews-reviews-google-search/3972510/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How LAUSD got here","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In September, LAUSD put a moratorium on student use of generative AI on district devices. At the start of the school year, Google helped the district turn off AI Mode, the chatbot-style search, for students signed in with district accounts. Even then, some searches could still show AI summaries, and the district had asked Google for a way to switch them off, LAist reported in early November.","sources":[{"name":"NBC Los Angeles","url":"https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/lausd-disables-google-ai-overviews-reviews-google-search/3972510/"},{"name":"LAist","url":"https://laist.com/news/education/lausd-google-artificial-intelligence-search-gemini"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A district spokesperson told NBC Los Angeles that disabling AI Overviews is part of LAUSD's ongoing effort to manage student access to new technology and keep their online experience age-appropriate and safe. The district said it continues to evaluate whether Google Search and other digital tools support student learning.","sources":[{"name":"NBC Los Angeles","url":"https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/lausd-disables-google-ai-overviews-reviews-google-search/3972510/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"LAUSD Chief Information Officer Jack Kelanic told a board committee that the district is not bound to Google's products and could change its default search engine overnight, according to Los Angeles Magazine. NBC Los Angeles, citing The New York Times, reported that districts weighing alternatives are looking at DuckDuckGo and Microsoft's Bing, which both offer ways to turn off AI answers.","sources":[{"name":"NBC Los Angeles","url":"https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/lausd-disables-google-ai-overviews-reviews-google-search/3972510/"},{"name":"Los Angeles Magazine","url":"https://lamag.com/education/l-a-schools-block-googles-ai-overview-despite-companys-latest-ai-policy/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Other districts and critics","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"New York City schools Chancellor Kamar H. Samuels said the city would explore other search options if Google does not reconsider, and Chicago Public Schools said it would look for other solutions if it cannot reach an agreement with Google. Hundreds of Google employees also signed a petition asking the company to let schools turn off AI features, and former Federal Trade Commission chair Lina Khan accused Google of using its search monopoly to coerce schools, Los Angeles Magazine reported.","sources":[{"name":"NBC Los Angeles","url":"https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/lausd-disables-google-ai-overviews-reviews-google-search/3972510/"},{"name":"Los Angeles Magazine","url":"https://lamag.com/education/l-a-schools-block-googles-ai-overview-despite-companys-latest-ai-policy/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The Los Angeles block weakens Google's main argument that AI and Search cannot be separated for schools. If one of the largest districts in the country can remove AI Overviews on its own, other districts that want Search without AI have a working example, and Google's opt-in rule looks more like a policy choice than a technical limit.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next signal is whether Google changes its K-12 policy before the default-off settings take effect, or whether New York City, Chicago or Los Angeles formally switches students to another search engine.","sources":[]}]}

Below are ten to copy, with [brackets] for your details.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Use chat in Gemini Notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16179559?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Before you prompt: set up the notebook","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Geekflare collected those examples from the team.","sources":[{"name":"Geekflare","url":"https://geekflare.com/news/notebooklm-prompts-you-can-use-right-now-for-better-summaries/"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 10: A Custom chat role","text":"Act as a strict tutor for [course]. Answer only from my sources, keep answers short, and after each answer ask me one follow-up question to check that I understood.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Paste this into Configure Chat under Custom. Google's own examples for Custom are a style like answering as a PhD student or a role like a game host, so a tutor role fits what the setting is meant for.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where NotebookLM prompts fall short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Grounding cuts down on invented facts, but it does not make the model a perfect reader. item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Turnitin AI checker: how it works, what the score means and its limits","dek":"Turnitin's AI writing indicator gives instructors a percentage of a paper's prose that AI tools may have written. Here is how to read it, what it needs to run, who can see it and what Turnitin says about false positives.","summary":"Turnitin's AI checker estimates how much of a paper's qualifying prose AI tools may have generated, highlights those parts and hides scores from 1 to 19 percent behind an asterisk. Turnitin says it aims for a false positive rate under 1 percent and that the score should never be the only basis for action against a student.","seo_title":"Turnitin AI checker: how it works, scores and false positives","seo_description":"How the Turnitin AI checker works: what the percentage and asterisk mean, the 300 word minimum, who sees it, and what Turnitin says about false positives.","answer_summary":"Turnitin's AI checker splits a paper into overlapping segments, scores each sentence and reports the share of qualifying prose it thinks AI may have written. Scores from 1 to 19 percent show only an asterisk, students cannot see the report, and Turnitin says the score is not proof of misconduct.","tags":["Turnitin","AI detection","AI writing","Students","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"The Turnitin AI checker, which Turnitin calls its AI writing indicator, shows instructors a percentage: how much of a submission's qualifying text AI tools such as ChatGPT may have generated. Qualifying text means prose sentences in long-form writing. Lists, bullet points and other text that is not in sentences are left out, so the number is not always a share of the whole paper.","sources":[{"name":"Turnitin: AI writing detection FAQ","url":"https://www.turnitin.com/products/features/ai-writing-detection/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The percentage links to an AI writing report that highlights the parts the model flagged. Cyan marks text that is likely AI-generated. Purple marks text that is likely AI-generated and was also likely run through an AI paraphrasing tool. The AI score is separate from the similarity score, and the AI highlights do not appear in the Similarity Report itself.","sources":[{"name":"Turnitin: AI writing detection FAQ","url":"https://www.turnitin.com/products/features/ai-writing-detection/"},{"name":"Turnitin Guides: AI writing detection in the enhanced Similarity Report view","url":"https://guides.ithenticate.com/hc/en-us/articles/27835303398541-AI-writing-detection-in-the-new-enhanced-Similarity-Report-view"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How the Turnitin AI checker works","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Turnitin says its detector is built on an open source foundation model and was first trained on output from GPT-3 and GPT-3.5, then extended to GPT-4, GPT-4o, Gemini Pro and LLaMA. It splits text into overlapping segments of about five to ten sentences and gives each sentence a score between 0 and 1. The paraphrase check only runs on segments the main detector has already flagged as AI-generated.","sources":[{"name":"Turnitin: AI writing detection FAQ","url":"https://www.turnitin.com/products/features/ai-writing-detection/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A file needs at least 300 words of prose, must be under 100 MB and must be a .docx, .pdf, .txt or .rtf file. Turnitin's pages give a maximum of 30,000 words, while a University of Melbourne guide updated in March 2026 lists 15,000, so check your own institution's setup. Turnitin's enhanced report guide lists several languages beyond English, but it says the paraphrase and bypasser checks only work in English.","sources":[{"name":"Turnitin: AI writing detection FAQ","url":"https://www.turnitin.com/products/features/ai-writing-detection/"},{"name":"Turnitin Guides: AI writing detection in the enhanced Similarity Report view","url":"https://guides.ithenticate.com/hc/en-us/articles/27835303398541-AI-writing-detection-in-the-new-enhanced-Similarity-Report-view"},{"name":"University of Melbourne: Accessing and interpreting the AI Writing Report","url":"https://lms.unimelb.edu.au/staff/guides/canvas/assignments/turnitin-accessing-and-interpreting-the-ai-writing-report"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to read your Turnitin AI score","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open the AI writing report","text":"In the classic report view, the AI indicator sits in the toolbar on the right. Selecting the percentage opens the AI writing report in a new tab. In the newer report view, look for the AI Writing tab in the top menu. Where it appears in your learning platform depends on how your school connected Turnitin.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Check which state the indicator is in","text":"A blue indicator with 0 or a number from 20 to 100 is a finished result. An asterisk next to the percent sign means the score landed between 1 and 19 percent. Turnitin shows no number and no highlights there because results in that range are less reliable and false positives are more likely. A gray indicator with two dashes means the file was not processed, and an error icon means processing failed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Read the highlights, not just the number","text":"Look at which passages are cyan or purple and whether they are long stretches of prose or short pieces. Turnitin says that in papers of only a few hundred words, the result is mostly all or nothing. The University of Melbourne advises reviewing the whole document rather than judging sentence by sentence.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Download the PDF to share it","text":"Students cannot see the indicator or the report. Instructors can download the report as a PDF from the button in the upper right and share it. The University of Melbourne guide says the PDF includes a cover sheet, a FAQ about the score and the highlighted essay.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you are a student and a teacher raises an AI score, ask to see that PDF. It shows exactly which passages were flagged, which is the only way to answer the concern line by line.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"False positives and what the score does not mean","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Turnitin says it aims to keep its false positive rate under 1 percent for documents with more than 20 percent AI writing, and that it might flag about one in every 100 fully human documents. To hold that rate, it says it may miss around 15 percent of AI-written text, so a paper showing 50 percent could contain more. The company lists lists with little variation, text that repeats itself and paraphrasing that adds no new ideas as things that can cause false positives.","sources":[{"name":"Turnitin: AI writing detection FAQ","url":"https://www.turnitin.com/products/features/ai-writing-detection/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Turnitin says simple spelling and grammar fixes in Grammarly are not flagged in most cases, but Grammarly's generative features and paraphrasers such as QuillBot will likely be flagged when used on AI text. It also says the score should not be the sole basis for action against a student and that Turnitin does not decide whether misconduct happened. The University of Melbourne says a high score alone is not grounds for an allegation.","sources":[{"name":"Turnitin: AI writing detection FAQ","url":"https://www.turnitin.com/products/features/ai-writing-detection/"},{"name":"Turnitin Guides: AI writing detection in the enhanced Similarity Report view","url":"https://guides.ithenticate.com/hc/en-us/articles/27835303398541-AI-writing-detection-in-the-new-enhanced-Similarity-Report-view"},{"name":"University of Melbourne: Turnitin's AI writing detection tool","url":"https://academicintegrity.unimelb.edu.au/staff-resources/turnitins-ai-writing-detection-tool"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Who gets the Turnitin AI checker","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"AI detection comes with Turnitin's Originality license or as an add-on for iThenticate 2.0. Schools with only the Similarity, Feedback Studio or Originality Check products do not get it, and administrators can turn it off. Gradescope has no AI detection. Older submissions are not scored after the fact, so they would need to be submitted again.","sources":[{"name":"Turnitin: AI writing detection FAQ","url":"https://www.turnitin.com/products/features/ai-writing-detection/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The Turnitin AI checker is built to start a conversation, and Turnitin says so in its own documentation. The asterisk under 20 percent, the 300 word minimum and the published miss rate all show a tool tuned to avoid accusing human writers, at the cost of missing some AI text. Treat the number as a reason to look closer, never as a verdict.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"A file with fewer than 300 words of prose gets no AI score, and lists or bullet points are left out of the count, so the checker says nothing about those parts of an assignment.","sources":[]}]}

Run Reference Check on your draft","text":"When your draft and reference list are stable, upload the manuscript to Reference Check. It shows how each reference has been cited and flags retractions, editorial notices and contrasting evidence. Scite describes it as a safety net, not proof that your review is rigorous.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Install the browser extension. After you log in, it shows a badge with the counts of supporting, mentioning and contrasting citations next to papers you read online, and clicking it opens the paper's page in Scite.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use Scite inside ChatGPT or Claude","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Scite offers connectors for ChatGPT and Claude, and its MCP server also works with Copilot, Cursor and other MCP clients. In ChatGPT you type @Scite to ground a question in Scite's data. The pricing page says MCP access needs a paid plan, an active trial or an Enterprise license, and Basic includes 250 MCP credits a month.","sources":[{"name":"Scite: Getting started","url":"https://scite.ai/getting-started"},{"name":"Scite blog: How to use AI for literature review","url":"https://scite.ai/blog/how-to-use-ai-for-literature-review"},{"name":"Scite pricing","url":"https://scite.ai/pricing.md"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Scite falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Coverage is the main limit. HKU Libraries points out that much scholarly content is still behind paywalls and that Scite's database is not exhaustive. Scite's own tutorial says it is not enough on its own for a systematic review. HKU also found an unrelated paper cited in an Assistant answer, and a result titled Untitled that still had a working DOI.","sources":[{"name":"Scite blog: How to use AI for literature review","url":"https://scite.ai/blog/how-to-use-ai-for-literature-review"},{"name":"HKU Libraries: Features and limitations of Scite Assistant and Scite MCP","url":"https://blog-sc.hku.hk/features-and-limitations-of-scite-assistant-and-scite-mcp/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Scite is strongest at the step most AI tools skip: showing what other researchers said about a paper after it came out. Use it to find and vet sources, not as the only search behind your review.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Before you cite anything Assistant found, open the paper and confirm it says what the summary claims. HKU Libraries says the outputs should not be treated as definitive.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: AI agent vs agentic AI: the difference in plain words
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: An AI agent does one specific task on its own: sort a ticket, check an invoice, answer a set question. It acts when told to and does not plan ahead. Agentic AI starts from a goal, breaks it into steps and coordinates several agents to finish it. IBM describes a conductor model that supervises simpler agents. Sources: Google Cloud: What is agentic AI?, IBM: What is agentic AI?, Workday: AI agents vs agentic AI, ISACA: AI agents and agentic AI, arXiv: AI Agents vs. Agentic AI (Sapkota, Roumeliotis, Karkee).

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"AI agent vs agentic AI: the difference in plain words, with examples","dek":"An AI agent does one task on its own. Agentic AI plans a goal and coordinates agents to reach it. Here is how to tell them apart and which one you need.","summary":"An AI agent is software that performs a specific task on its own, while agentic AI is a system that sets a goal, plans the steps and coordinates several agents with little supervision. Google Cloud, IBM and ISACA draw the line in similar places, and ISACA advises using the simplest option that works.","seo_title":"AI agent vs agentic AI: the difference in plain words","seo_description":"AI agent vs agentic AI explained: the 4 real differences, where experts disagree, when to pick each one, and 3 prompts to sort your own work into agent tasks.","answer_summary":"An AI agent performs one specific task on its own. Agentic AI is a larger system that sets a goal, plans the steps and coordinates one or more agents to reach it with limited human supervision.","tags":["AI agents","Agentic AI","Google Cloud","IBM","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"AI agent vs agentic AI sounds like a word game, but the two terms describe different things. An AI agent is a piece of software built to do a specific task on its own. Agentic AI is the bigger system: it sets a goal, plans the steps, and coordinates one or more agents to get there with little human help. That is how Google Cloud and IBM both describe it on their own explainer pages.","sources":[{"name":"Google Cloud: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-agentic-ai"},{"name":"IBM: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/agentic-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google Cloud puts it in one line: an AI agent might focus on a specific task, while agentic AI employs multiple agents to handle complex workflows. Google's comparison is a toolbox. The agents are the individual tools, and agentic AI is the coordinated use of those tools to finish a job.","sources":[{"name":"Google Cloud: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-agentic-ai"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"AI agent vs agentic AI: the short definitions","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"AI agent: Google Cloud calls agents autonomous entities designed to perform specific tasks. Workday, the HR and finance software company, describes them as task oriented systems that carry out predefined actions within a workflow, such as answering an HR question or checking finance data. They act when given an instruction and do not plan ahead on their own.","sources":[{"name":"Google Cloud: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-agentic-ai"},{"name":"Workday: AI agents vs agentic AI","url":"https://www.workday.com/en-gb/perspectives/ai/understanding-the-difference-between-ai-agents-and-agentic-ai.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Agentic AI: IBM defines it as an AI system that can accomplish a specific goal with limited supervision, and says it is made of AI agents. Google Cloud describes it as focused on autonomous decision making and action: it can set goals, plan and carry out tasks with minimal human intervention, using a large language model as the brain and acting through tools.","sources":[{"name":"Google Cloud: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-agentic-ai"},{"name":"IBM: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/agentic-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Workday's shorthand is the easiest to remember: agentic AI is the thinker, AI agents are the doers. A 2025 research paper by Ranjan Sapkota, Konstantinos Roumeliotis and Manoj Karkee draws the line in a similar place. It treats AI agents as single, task specific systems and agentic AI as several specialized agents that coordinate, with shared memory and task breakdown.","sources":[{"name":"Workday: AI agents vs agentic AI","url":"https://www.workday.com/en-gb/perspectives/ai/understanding-the-difference-between-ai-agents-and-agentic-ai.html"},{"name":"arXiv: AI Agents vs. Agentic AI (Sapkota, Roumeliotis, Karkee)","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2505.10468v4"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The 4 differences that actually matter","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Scope: one task or one goal","text":"An agent does one job well: sort the support ticket, pull the invoice, draft the reply. An agentic system starts from a goal, such as resolving a customer complaint end to end, and decides which tasks it needs. Google Cloud's list of uses for agentic AI includes customer service, supply chains and software development.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Planning: follow steps or make them","text":"Workday says plainly that agents do not plan ahead and do not choose between alternatives. Agentic AI breaks a goal into steps and picks the order. IBM describes this as a goal setting stage that uses planning methods before the system acts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Coordination: alone or as a team","text":"IBM describes multiagent systems where each agent handles one subtask and their work is coordinated through orchestration. One design it describes uses a conductor model, powered by an LLM, that supervises simpler agents. A single agent has no one to coordinate with.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Learning: same every time or improving","text":"IBM lists learning and adaptation as a step in how agentic systems work, using feedback from earlier results. Google Cloud calls the same stage reflection. ISACA lists memory and knowledge management among the parts an agentic system needs.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where the experts disagree","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Not everyone uses the words the same way, and you will see it in product pages. ISACA, the IT governance association, points out that being an agent does not automatically mean being autonomous. A basic customer service chatbot is technically an agent but has no real agency. In ISACA's framing, agentic AI is defined by agency, the ability to act on its own, rather than by the number of agents.","sources":[{"name":"ISACA: AI agents and agentic AI","url":"https://isaca.org/resources/news-and-trends/isaca-now-blog/2025/ai-agents-and-agentic-ai-understanding-the-difference-that-matters-for-your-organization"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"So when a company says its product is agentic, ask what it actually decides on its own. If it only runs a fixed script after you press a button, it is an agent, or simply automation, whatever the marketing says.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Which one you need for your work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"ISACA's advice is practical: use the simplest solution that works, and it says that might mean not building agentic systems at all. Simpler agents are more cost effective. IBM adds the risks that come with more autonomy: a system rewarded for a score can exploit loopholes to hit it in ways nobody intended, and when many agents work together one failure can cascade through the rest.","sources":[{"name":"ISACA: AI agents and agentic AI","url":"https://isaca.org/resources/news-and-trends/isaca-now-blog/2025/ai-agents-and-agentic-ai-understanding-the-difference-that-matters-for-your-organization"},{"name":"IBM: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/agentic-ai"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"Pick an agent when","text":"The task is the same every time, the steps are known, and a mistake is easy to spot. Examples: tagging emails, filling a form from a document, answering a set list of HR questions.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"Pick an agentic system when","text":"The goal is clear but the path is not, the job crosses several apps, and the work is worth the extra checking. Examples: researching a topic across many sources, handling a support case from start to refund, or a coding task that needs planning, editing and testing.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Keep a human in the loop either way. Google Cloud's own page recommends human oversight for agentic AI, and ISACA notes that autonomy reduces the need for supervision but does not remove it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"3 prompts to sort your own work","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Split a job into agent tasks","text":"Here is a task I do every week: [describe the task in 3 to 5 sentences]. Break it into the smallest separate steps. For each step, tell me: is the input always the same format, does it need a judgment call, and what would go wrong if an AI got it wrong. Then group the steps into ones a simple AI agent could do and ones that need a person or a planning system.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Test an agentic claim","text":"A vendor says this product is agentic: [paste the product description]. Based only on this text, list what the product decides on its own, what it does only when a person tells it to, and what tools or apps it can act in. Say which parts are unclear and give me 5 questions to ask the vendor.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Plan the checks","text":"I want an AI system to handle this goal with little supervision: [describe the goal]. List the points where it should stop and ask me before acting, the actions it should never take on its own, and how I would notice if it took a shortcut to look successful.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The useful takeaway is simple. AI agent describes a worker with one job. Agentic AI describes a system that plans and runs a whole job, often with several of those workers. Both terms are stretched in marketing, so judge a product by what it decides on its own, not by the label.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How the Mercor AI interview works, and how to prepare
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The Practice Interview is free, can be repeated and is never shown to companies. The real one takes about 20 minutes. Use Chrome on a computer. A working mic is required, plus full screen sharing when asked. Face in frame and good light make a clear recording. Long silences make the AI jump in. If it cuts you off, say you were not finished. Using an AI to write your answers is banned. Sources: Mercor docs: AI Interview, Mercor docs: Apply for a Job, Mercor docs: How Mercor Uses AI and Data, Mercor blog: Engineering Monty.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to pass the Mercor AI interview: setup, rules, retakes and what happens to your data","dek":"Mercor screens every candidate with an AI interviewer called Monty. Here is how it works, what to set up first, what is banned, and how the three retakes work.","summary":"Mercor's AI interviewer asks role specific questions built from your resume and the job description, and most interviews take about 20 minutes. It is the only screening method, you get up to three retakes, and only your latest attempt is evaluated.","seo_title":"How to pass the Mercor AI interview: setup, rules and retakes","seo_description":"How the Mercor AI interview works: the free practice run, the setup checks, what AI help is banned, how the three retakes work and what Mercor keeps.","answer_summary":"The Mercor AI interview is a roughly 20 minute conversation with an AI interviewer that asks questions based on your resume and the role. Take the free practice interview, use Chrome on a computer with a working mic and camera, answer clearly, and save your three retakes for technical problems.","tags":["Mercor","AI interview","AI jobs","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to pass the Mercor AI interview starts with knowing what it is. Mercor is a hiring platform that matches experts with paid projects, and its help center says every candidate is screened by an AI interviewer that asks questions about the role, makes a transcript and scores your answers for that listing. Most interviews take about 20 minutes, and you only need to finish each one once.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There is no human alternative. Mercor's docs say the AI interview is the only screening method, and it cannot be done by chat, phone call or any other format. Mercor's engineering blog names the interviewer Monty and says it runs around 10,000 conversations a day, about fifteen minutes each on average, across hundreds of job categories.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: Apply for a Job","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/how-to/apply"},{"name":"Mercor blog: Engineering Monty","url":"https://www.mercor.com/blog/monty-engineering-deep-dive/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the Mercor AI interview asks you","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Mercor, the interviewer builds its questions from your resume and the job description, then transcribes and evaluates what you say. Some interviews are technical, others test language or reasoning. The blog post adds that the most common one, a general Domain Expert interview, makes up more than 70% of sessions, and that coding problems are generated from your profile.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: How Mercor Uses AI and Data","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/policies/data-ai-usage"},{"name":"Mercor blog: Engineering Monty","url":"https://www.mercor.com/blog/monty-engineering-deep-dive/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"If you pass an interview, the result carries over. Mercor calls this assessment reuse: a passed assessment does not need to be taken again for comparable roles, and a finished interview is kept when another application asks for the same one.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: Apply for a Job","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/how-to/apply"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Before you start: setup that actually matters","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Do the free practice interview","text":"Mercor offers a Practice Interview that is not tied to any application, does not affect your chances and can be repeated as often as you like. Practice interviews are not shared with companies, so use one to get used to the format.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Use Chrome on a computer","text":"Mercor recommends the latest Google Chrome. Edge and Safari are supported, Firefox is not. Some interviews need a computer; on a phone you will see a message saying the interview needs one, with a button to copy the link and open it on a laptop.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Pass the setup checks","text":"In the waiting room, the Setup checks tab tests your devices. Working mic is required, and so is screen sharing when the interview asks for it (share your entire screen, not one tab). Face in frame, good lighting, a working camera and a steady camera are not required, but Mercor says you need them for a clear recording. If Start interview stays gray, one required check has failed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Pick a quiet room","text":"Mercor suggests a quiet space, a stable connection, headphones and an external mic. Keep your whole face visible. Interviews are in English unless the listing says otherwise. Pen and paper help, plus a calculator for number heavy roles.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"During the interview","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Speak clearly and keep answers tight. Mercor warns that long silences can make the AI jump in. If it interrupts you while you are thinking, the docs say you can simply tell it you were not finished.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Captions are on by default and can be turned off. Some interviews include a whiteboard that saves on its own. If something breaks, use the Help button inside the interview. If the bot stops answering, Mercor's checklist is to wait 30 to 60 seconds, refresh and rejoin, clear Chrome's cached files and cookies, and turn off VPNs, ad blockers and privacy extensions.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On AI help, the rules are strict. Mercor's LLM usage policy, as summarized in its interview FAQ, allows grammar and wording checks but bans using large language models to write your answers, rate model responses, write explanations or review code. The docs also ask candidates not to share specific questions or screenshots of the interview.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Retakes: you get three","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You can retake an interview up to three times across all applications that use it. Open the Assessments tab, click Retake assessment on the interview card, pick a reason (the options include Technical issue, Interrupted and Improve performance) and click Retake interview. Only your most recent attempt is evaluated, and retaking resets your application progress.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: Apply for a Job","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/how-to/apply"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Save retakes for real problems. Mercor's own waiting room note says hiring managers can see how many times you retook an interview. An attempt that ends far too early is marked Interview too short and does not count, but retaking it still uses one of your three.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"After you submit","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Your application shows Ready to submit or Submitted for each step. Mercor gives no timeline for results; you are told when the application moves to the next stage, and you can keep applying elsewhere. Mercor says it cannot give specific feedback on rejections because of volume, and a submitted application cannot be edited or withdrawn.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: Apply for a Job","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/how-to/apply"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On data, Mercor keeps the video, audio and transcript of official interviews to judge your candidacy and recommend you to employers, and says it does not sell interview data. Its FAQ says interview data will not be used to train AI models; its data policy says the data does train Mercor's internal recommendation models but never third party language models. You cannot download your recording or transcript. You can delete your account and its data in Account Settings, unless you have an active contract, a payout in progress or an open offer.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: How Mercor Uses AI and Data","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/policies/data-ai-usage"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The honest read: there is no trick to beat the Mercor AI interview. The interviewer works from your resume, so the best preparation is a clean, text based PDF resume that states your real experience, one practice run, and a setup that passes every check. Mercor's own resume rules ask for a PDF under 2 MB, one or two pages, with no images or tables.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: NotebookLM vs Gemini: which one to use for your files
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Gemini Notebook answers only from the files you upload, with citations. Use it when a made up fact would hurt you. The Gemini app opens the same notebooks but may also use web search and other tools. Use it for anything your files do not cover. item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"NotebookLM vs Gemini: which one to use for your files, and when to use both","dek":"NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook, and its notebooks also open in the Gemini app. One answers only from your sources, the other can add the web.","summary":"Gemini Notebook, the new name for NotebookLM, answers only from the sources in a notebook and holds the Studio tools such as Audio Overviews and flashcards. Use the Gemini app when you want your notebook plus web search.","tags":["Gemini Notebook","NotebookLM","Gemini","Google","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"NotebookLM vs Gemini comes down to one choice: answers only from your own files, or answers that may also use the web. Google's help pages now call NotebookLM Gemini Notebook, an AI research assistant that answers from the sources you upload, with in-line citations. The Gemini app is the general assistant, and since this year it can open the same notebooks.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"},{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Learn about Gemini Notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16164461"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version: use Gemini Notebook when the answer must stay inside your documents and you want study tools like Audio Overviews, flashcards and quizzes. Use the Gemini app when you want to mix your notebook with web search and Gemini's other tools. The notebooks themselves are shared between the two apps, so you do not have to pick only one.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16972047"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"NotebookLM vs Gemini: the one difference that matters","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google's own help page states it plainly. In Gemini Notebook, answers are grounded only in your notebook sources. In the Gemini app, answers are grounded in your notebook sources but may also include web search and other tools. Gemini Notebook is designed to answer from the information in what you uploaded, and every answer carries citations you can click back to the source.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"},{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Learn about Gemini Notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16164461"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Chalkbox, a study site that tested both, sums it up the same way: the notebook answers only from your sources, the app answers from everything. It also adds a fair warning: grounding cuts down on made up facts, but the model can still misread a document. Check the citation before you quote anything.","sources":[{"name":"Chalkbox","url":"https://www.chalkbox.org/guides/notebooklm-vs-gemini/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"That makes the choice easy in practice. Writing about assigned readings, a contract, or meeting notes where a made up fact would hurt you: Gemini Notebook. Explaining a concept your files do not cover, or checking something against the current web: the Gemini app.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How notebooks work across both apps","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Notebooks you create in Gemini Notebook now show up automatically in the Gemini app's navigation, and you can view, edit and chat with them from either side. Renaming a notebook, adding sources, or changing its custom instructions syncs between the two apps. If a change does not show up, Google suggests refreshing. Both apps share one set of custom instructions per notebook.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There are a few catches. Shared notebooks made in Gemini Notebook, even ones you own, do not appear in the Gemini app. A notebook that contains Gemini chats is private and cannot be shared. Play Books ebooks can only be added as sources in Gemini Notebook. In the European Economic Area you have to connect Gemini Notebook to Gemini by hand; in most other regions it connects automatically.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16972047"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What only Gemini Notebook can do","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Studio panel is the big reason to open Gemini Notebook itself. Google lists Notes, Audio Overviews, Video Overviews, Mind Maps, Reports (FAQ, study guide or briefing document, with Export to Docs), Data Tables (Export to Sheets), Flashcards, Quizzes, Slide Decks and Infographics. The Gemini app cannot generate these Studio items: Google says they are only available in Gemini Notebook.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"},{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16206563"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Audio Overviews turn your sources into a discussion between AI hosts. You can pick Deep Dive (the default), The Brief (one speaker, under two minutes), The Critique or The Debate, choose the length, and add a prompt about what to focus on. In English you can also use Interactive mode and join the conversation to ask questions. It works in more than 80 languages.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Audio Overview","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16212820"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Flashcards and Quizzes turn your sources into study aids. You can set the difficulty to easy, medium or hard, choose fewer, standard or more cards, and add a prompt. Flashcards have Got it! and Missed it! buttons, so you can review only the cards you missed, and you can download the deck as a CSV file.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Flashcards or Quizzes","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16958963"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the Gemini app adds","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In the Gemini app, a notebook chat can use web searches and any Gemini tool, and Gemini remembers the context of your sources and instructions. item.title: How to use Krea for free: images, video and upscaling
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Every image costs compute units. Krea 2 Turbo costs 2, Flux 5, Nano Banana 114. Free users get a small amount each day. Pick a model, add a start and end image if you like, set length and resolution, then Generate. Hover a clip and click Extend to go longer. Realtime updates the picture as you draw, type or move in front of your webcam. No render button. Sources: Krea docs: What is Krea?, Krea docs: Image generation, Krea docs: Video generation, Krea docs: Enhancer, Krea docs: Realtime, Krea docs: Compute units, Krea docs: Agent plans and credits.

item.title: Nvidia just stopped shipping AI servers to four Asian countries
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Dell and Supermicro told customers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that Nvidia will not authorize their orders, the FT reports. Nvidia declined to comment. New US rules give regional cloud providers 90 days to get export licenses and prove no restricted users. The target: Chinese developers renting Nvidia compute nearby. Sources: The National, Lowyat.NET.

item.title: OpenAI admits a billing mistake: ChatGPT users will now hit GPT-6.2 limits 40% faster
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux wrote on X that a billing mistake at the GPT-6.2 launch on November 17 discounted Astra and Sol usage for most users. The fix is live. That cut CPU use by about 8 to 10 percent, which the team judged too small to justify the added complexity, The Terminal reported. The full rewrite was reconsidered as Claude improved at coding.","sources":[{"name":"The Terminal","url":"https://theterminal.space/software/anthropic-messages-api-rust-70-percent-cpu"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude wrote the first version of the core request path in about a week, according to The Neuron, while confirming that it actually worked took months. By May 2026, Claude was writing more than 80 percent of merged code, and the number of merged changes per two-week period rose from under 100 to over 3,000 by August, The Terminal reported.","sources":[{"name":"The Neuron","url":"https://www.theneuron.ai/news/anthropic-claude-api-rust-migration/"},{"name":"The Terminal","url":"https://theterminal.space/software/anthropic-messages-api-rust-70-percent-cpu"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Passing tests turned out to be a weak signal. By April 2026 the Rust version passed about 98 percent of roughly 700 existing integration tests, but only about a quarter of real production inputs produced matching results. An audit found more than 100 test assertions that had been weakened during the port. The match rate reached 99.6 percent before the cutover, according to The Terminal.","sources":[{"name":"The Neuron","url":"https://www.theneuron.ai/news/anthropic-claude-api-rust-migration/"},{"name":"The Terminal","url":"https://theterminal.space/software/anthropic-messages-api-rust-70-percent-cpu"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"To compare the two systems, engineers sent the same requests through both versions. The model ran once and its output was shared with both implementations, because Claude can answer the same question differently. Differences were recorded without engineers reading customer conversations. When a new kind of mismatch appeared, a coordinating agent assigned another agent to reproduce it, test a fix and send the fix to an engineer for review.","sources":[{"name":"The Neuron","url":"https://www.theneuron.ai/news/anthropic-claude-api-rust-migration/"},{"name":"The Terminal","url":"https://theterminal.space/software/anthropic-messages-api-rust-70-percent-cpu"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Human review still caught shortcuts. In one case an agent proposed copying a missing web search tool description into local files. The fix passed the automated checks, but an engineer rejected it because the API needed to fetch that description from an internal service. The feedback was saved as an instruction for future agents, The Neuron reported.","sources":[{"name":"The Neuron","url":"https://www.theneuron.ai/news/anthropic-claude-api-rust-migration/"},{"name":"The Terminal","url":"https://theterminal.space/software/anthropic-messages-api-rust-70-percent-cpu"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The reported results","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic reports about 70 percent less CPU usage and more than 80 percent less memory per request, plus a 20 percent cut in median time to first token for Claude Code requests. The Terminal noted that these figures have not been checked outside the company and that an October podcast summary gave smaller numbers for the service layer.","sources":[{"name":"The Neuron","url":"https://www.theneuron.ai/news/anthropic-claude-api-rust-migration/"},{"name":"The Terminal","url":"https://theterminal.space/software/anthropic-messages-api-rust-70-percent-cpu"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The most useful lesson in the report is about checking, not writing. Generating a full rewrite was fast, but the gap between a 98 percent test pass rate and a 25 percent match on real traffic shows how misleading green tests can be when an AI is also editing them. Teams planning similar ports will likely spend most of their effort on comparison tooling and review rules rather than on the code itself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Watch whether other large software companies publish similar AI-led rewrites with match-rate data, which would show whether Anthropic's verification approach works outside its own systems.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Framer AI to build a website from a prompt
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open the Agent tab in a new project and say what the site is for, which sections it needs and the style. The agent builds real pages you can edit. item.title: How to use Ideogram for free: images with readable text
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Type a prompt like a poster that says "Summer Sale". Ideogram's docs say quoted text near the start comes out most reliably. English works best for text. Magic Prompt starts on and rewrites your prompt for richer images. Switch it off when you need the model to follow your exact words. item.title: How to use Gumloop to build an AI agent
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Click New agent, describe the job or pick a template, then add connectors like Gmail or Slack. Choose the model and click Save. Open the Triggers tab: an app event, a webhook, a schedule or a one-time run. Then the agent works without you starting it. Every task shows what it cost. One credit is half a cent. Start on Balanced or Auto and save the smartest model for hard jobs. Failed tool calls are not charged. If you run out, you can turn on overage billing at the same $0.005 per credit.","sources":[{"name":"Gumloop docs: Credits","url":"https://docs.gumloop.com/core-concepts/credits"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Bring your own API key (BYOK) needs Pro or higher. item.title: The U.S. just let SpaceX launch 1 million satellites that work as AI data centers in space
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The FCC approved SpaceX's plan on November 25 for up to 1 million solar powered compute satellites. About 17,000 satellites are in space today, Reuters reports, so this would be a huge jump. SpaceX must have a first satellite working by 2033, 10% of the fleet by 2035 and half by 2038. Amazon, Viasat and the American Astronomical Society opposed the plan. Starship launch at Starbase, Texas, September 2026. Each first generation unit carries Nvidia Vera Rubin class compute, rated up to 250 kW at peak. Sources: Reuters (via The Business Standard), Latin Times, Lynnwood Times.

SpaceX once sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites before it started that system, and operators often ask for more satellites than they end up launching.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters (via The Business Standard)","url":"https://www.tbsnews.net/worldbiz/usa/us-authorises-spacex-deploy-1-million-satellites-data-centres-space-1615466"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the satellites carry","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Lynnwood Times, the first generation unit, called AI1, has a deployed height of about 30 meters, a solar array wingspan of up to 75 meters and a mass of up to 4,000 kilograms. Each carries Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 class computing hardware rated up to 250 kilowatts at peak and about 175 kilowatts on average, cooled by liquid radiators and grouped in clusters of about 10 units.","sources":[{"name":"Lynnwood Times","url":"https://lynnwoodtimes.com/2026/11/25/starmind/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The satellites will fly in shells between 500 and 1,002 kilometers, in sun-synchronous and 30-degree orbits, and talk to each other and to Starlink over optical links. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr rejected that criticism in March, Reuters reported, and the commission dismissed the astronomers' concerns as outside the scope of the proceeding, according to Latin Times.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters (via The Business Standard)","url":"https://www.tbsnews.net/worldbiz/usa/us-authorises-spacex-deploy-1-million-satellites-data-centres-space-1615466"},{"name":"Latin Times","url":"https://www.latintimes.com/fcc-authorizes-spacex-starmind-ai-satellites-601871"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"One question remains open. item.title: How to use Devin, the AI software engineer
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Switch to Ask, pick your repo and ask how the code works. Ask mode never changes code. Then click Construct a Devin Prompt and Send to Devin. In Agent mode, choose the repository and the agent: Lite for chores, Normal by default, Ultra for the hardest work. Devin opens the pull request and watches CI. Sources: Devin docs: Introducing Devin, Devin docs: Your First Session, Devin docs: Self-serve plans, Cognition blog: New self-serve plans for Devin.

item.title: AI ads promised a Christmas wonderland. Shoppers found leak buckets
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The Kernow Christmas Market in Pool, Cornwall, was advertised with AI images of rows of stalls under lights, garlands and wreaths. They also showed an ice rink and a lodge bar with sofas and a stage. One of the AI-generated advert images. The market opened on November 20 in a mostly empty hall, with five buckets catching water from a leak. One visitor counted only five stalls and said there were "no decorations, no lights." A vendor who paid £30 a day called it an "absolute shambles." Sources: Mirror UK (via AOL), Capital Digest, AI Weekly.

item.title: How to use Jules, Google's coding agent
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Sign in at jules.google.com, connect GitHub, pick a repo and branch, then describe the task. Click Give me a plan. Jules works in its own cloud VM. Open each step and reply in the chat if something is off. Then approve the plan. Leave the page and Jules approves it on its own after a timer. Sources: Jules docs: Getting started, Jules docs: Limits and Plans, Jules docs: Environment setup, Jules docs: Jules Tools CLI reference, Jules docs: API quickstart, Jules docs: Reviewing the plan, Google blog: New ways to build with Jules, TechRepublic.
