item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Jules, Google's coding agent: your first task, the plans and the CLI","dek":"Jules takes a GitHub repo and a plain request, writes a plan and does the work in its own cloud machine. Here are the steps, task prompts to start with and what each plan allows.","summary":"Jules is Google's experimental coding agent: it connects to GitHub, plans a change and carries it out in a short lived virtual machine. The base plan allows 15 tasks a day and 3 at once, Jules in Pro 100 and 15, and Jules in Ultra 300 and 60.","seo_title":"How to use Jules: Google's AI coding agent, step by step","seo_description":"How to use Jules, Google's coding agent: connect GitHub, write a task, approve the plan, set up your environment and use the CLI, plus each plan's daily limits.","answer_summary":"Sign in at jules.google.com, connect your GitHub account, pick a repository and branch, describe the task and click Give me a plan. Review and approve the plan, and Jules does the work in a cloud VM. The base plan allows 15 tasks a day.","tags":["Jules","Google","AI coding agent","GitHub","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you want to know how to use Jules, here is the short version: sign in with your Google account, connect GitHub, pick a repository, describe what you want, and approve the plan Jules writes. Google's docs call Jules an experimental coding agent that fixes bugs, adds documentation and builds features, and that works on its own once you hand it a task.","sources":[{"name":"Jules docs: Getting started","url":"https://jules.google/docs"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The key difference from a chat assistant is where the work happens. Each task runs in a secure, short lived virtual machine where Jules clones your code, installs dependencies and edits files. You do not have to keep a window open while it works, which is why Google's blog describes it as an agent for generating code, fixing bugs, writing tests and improving performance.","sources":[{"name":"Jules docs: Getting started","url":"https://jules.google/docs"},{"name":"Jules docs: Environment setup","url":"https://jules.google/docs/environment/"},{"name":"Google blog: New ways to build with Jules","url":"https://blog.google/technology/google-labs/jules-tools-jules-api/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Jules: your first task","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Sign in","text":"Go to jules.google.com and sign in with your Google account. The first time, you accept a privacy notice. The docs say users must be 18 or older.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Connect GitHub","text":"Click Connect to GitHub account and finish the GitHub login. You can give Jules access to all your repositories or only the ones you choose. If you are not sent back to Jules afterward, refresh the page.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Pick the repository and branch","text":"Use the repo selector to choose a repository. The default branch is selected for you; change it if the work belongs on another branch.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Write a clear task","text":"Type the task in the prompt box. The docs ask for a clear, specific prompt, and their own example is a request to add a test for one named function in one named file. Name files and functions when you can.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Ask for a plan","text":"Click Give me a plan. Jules writes a plan before it touches any code. Turn on browser notifications when asked, or later under Settings, so you know when it needs you.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Review and approve the plan","text":"Expand each step of the plan. If something is wrong or missing, say so in the chat box, answer any questions Jules asks, and click approve plan when it looks right. One thing to know: if you leave the page, Jules approves the plan on its own after a timer, so check plans for risky tasks right away.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Task prompts to start with","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Add missing tests","text":"Add unit tests for the [function name] function in [file path]. Cover the normal case, empty input and invalid input. Use the test framework this repo already uses and do not change the function itself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Fix one bug","text":"Users report that [describe the bug, with the exact error message]. Find the cause, fix it with the smallest change that works, and add a test that fails before the fix and passes after it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Write documentation","text":"Read the code in [folder] and update README.md with a short section on how to install the project, how to run it locally and how to run the tests. Only describe commands that exist in this repo.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Small, specific tasks work better than one big request. Each task counts toward your daily limit, but a plan you can read in a minute is far easier to check than a long one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Set up the environment and AGENTS.md","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For simple repositories, Jules works out the setup itself and may read AGENTS.md or README.md for hints. For anything more complex, add a setup script: click the repository in the left sidebar, open Configuration at the top, and enter your commands in the Initial Setup box, for example an install command followed by your test command.","sources":[{"name":"Jules docs: Environment setup","url":"https://jules.google/docs/environment/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Click Run and Snapshot to test the script. When it succeeds, Jules saves a snapshot and reuses it for future tasks in that repository. Run to Validate checks the script without that step, which is useful for printing tool versions. The VM runs Ubuntu with Node.js, Bun, Python, Go, Java and Rust already installed, along with tools such as Docker. The docs advise keeping the script light and including install, lint and test commands.","sources":[{"name":"Jules docs: Environment setup","url":"https://jules.google/docs/environment/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Jules also looks for a file named AGENTS.md in the root of your repository and uses it to understand your code and plan better. The docs recommend keeping it up to date, so it is worth writing down your build commands, code style and anything the agent should never touch.","sources":[{"name":"Jules docs: Getting started","url":"https://jules.google/docs"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Jules limits and plans","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Limits and Plans page lists three tiers. The base Jules plan allows 15 tasks in a rolling 24 hours and 3 tasks at the same time, with Gemini 2.5 Pro. Jules in Pro, included with Google AI Pro, allows 100 tasks a day and 15 at once with higher access to the latest model, starting with Gemini 3 Pro. Jules in Ultra, included with Google AI Ultra, allows 300 tasks a day and 60 at once with priority access.","sources":[{"name":"Jules docs: Limits and Plans","url":"https://jules.google/docs/usage-limits/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When you hit the limit, the new task button is disabled until the limit resets, but you can still review and manage existing tasks. The paid tiers are currently only for individual Google accounts ending in @gmail.com, limits are not shared in a family plan, and Google says the limits may change. The page does not list prices.","sources":[{"name":"Jules docs: Limits and Plans","url":"https://jules.google/docs/usage-limits/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use Jules from the terminal or the API","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Jules Tools is a command line companion that Google announced on its blog. The docs install it with npm install -g @google/jules, and jules login opens a browser to sign in. Running jules with no arguments opens a dashboard in the terminal with a side by side diff viewer.","sources":[{"name":"Jules docs: Jules Tools CLI reference","url":"https://jules.google/docs/cli/reference"},{"name":"Google blog: New ways to build with Jules","url":"https://blog.google/technology/google-labs/jules-tools-jules-api/"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Jules Tools: the commands you will use most","text":"jules remote new --repo . --session \"write unit tests for the parser\"\njules remote list --session\njules remote pull --session [session id]","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The first command starts a task on the repository in your current folder, the second lists your sessions, and the third pulls the code changes from a finished session. A --parallel option on remote new runs several copies of a task at once.","sources":[{"name":"Jules docs: Jules Tools CLI reference","url":"https://jules.google/docs/cli/reference"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There is also a REST API, which the docs label an alpha release. You create up to three API keys on the Jules settings page, and sessions started through the API have their plans approved automatically unless you ask for approval. Setting automationMode to AUTO_CREATE_PR makes Jules open a pull request; by default it does not. Google's blog gives examples such as starting a task when a bug is filed in Slack or wiring Jules into a CI/CD pipeline.","sources":[{"name":"Jules docs: API quickstart","url":"https://jules.google/docs/api/reference/"},{"name":"Google blog: New ways to build with Jules","url":"https://blog.google/technology/google-labs/jules-tools-jules-api/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Jules is not good at","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Jules is built for tasks you can hand off and check later, not for quick back and forth while you code. Google still calls it experimental and the API is alpha, so features and limits can change. The auto approve timer means you should not start a risky task and walk away. And 15 tasks a day on the base plan goes fast if you split work into many small requests, so save it for jobs where a reviewed plan really saves you time.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start with a repository that has tests. Jules can run them in its VM, and a passing test suite is the quickest way for you to trust the change before you merge it.","sources":[]}]}

Use Chat for quick questions and Work for multi-step tasks, which shows you a plan to approve before it starts.","tags":["Le Chat","Mistral AI","Mistral Vibe","AI assistant","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you are looking up how to use Le Chat, the first thing to know is that it has a new name. On May 28, 2026, Mistral AI renamed Le Chat to Vibe, its single assistant for everyday work and for coding. Mistral's help center says your account, plan, conversations and saved content carried over, and you still sign in with the same login at chat.mistral.ai.","sources":[{"name":"Mistral help center: Le Chat is now Vibe","url":"https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/682992-le-chat-is-now-vibe"},{"name":"Mistral AI: Vibe announcement","url":"https://mistral.ai/it/news/vibe-agent/"},{"name":"The Decoder: Mistral rebrands Le Chat as Vibe","url":"https://the-decoder.com/mistral-rebrands-lechat-as-vibe-betting-its-chatbots-future-is-as-a-full-blown-work-agent/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Le Chat first launched in February 2024, and iOS and Android apps followed in February 2025. Mistral describes it as a multilingual assistant that can search the web, generate images, write and debug code, summarize documents or simply talk. The help center says it chooses its tools based on what you ask, so you do not have to switch them on for each question.","sources":[{"name":"Mistral help center: What is Le Chat and how do I use it","url":"https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347453-what-is-le-chat-and-how-do-i-use-it"},{"name":"Wikipedia: Mistral Vibe","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_Vibe"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Le Chat in its new Vibe form","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Sign in at chat.mistral.ai or in the app","text":"Open chat.mistral.ai in a browser, or install the app from the App Store or Google Play. If you had a Le Chat account, use the same login and your old conversations are there. Mistral's help center notes that some features need you to be logged in, so create an account even if you only plan to use the free plan.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose Chat or Work","text":"Vibe has three modes. Chat is the turn by turn conversation Le Chat was known for. Work is for tasks with several steps across your apps and files. Code is for developers. In heise's hands on test, logged in free users switched between Chat and Work with a control in the top left corner of the start screen. Mistral's announcement says Chat mode will be retired, with Le Chat history staying available in Work mode.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Write the full task, not a keyword","text":"Mistral's help center says the assistant has no prior context about you, so give it specific instructions. Say what you want, what to work from and what the answer should look like. Short keyword queries get generic answers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A news brief with sources","text":"Search the web for news about [topic] from the last 7 days. Give me 5 bullet points, each with one source link. End with one sentence on what to watch next. Leave out anything older than 7 days.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Upload a file and ask about it","text":"Mistral lists document and image understanding among the core features: you upload a file or picture and ask questions about it. For files you want to reuse, Libraries act as personal knowledge bases you can chat with, and Projects group related chats into folders.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Pull the key facts out of a document","text":"Read the attached [contract / report / PDF]. List every date, amount and deadline it mentions in a table with three columns: item, value, page. Then tell me in three sentences what I need to do and by when.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Hand a multi-step job to Work mode","text":"Work mode is where Vibe differs most from the old Le Chat. According to Mistral, it writes a plan and asks for your approval before it starts, works across connected apps such as Google Workspace, Outlook, SharePoint, Slack and GitHub, and streams its progress. You can expand each tool call to see what went in and what came out. Tasks can also run on a schedule: once, daily, weekly or monthly, with a notification when they finish.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A weekly task for Work mode","text":"Every Monday, read the spreadsheet [file name] and compare this week's [sales / signups / expenses] with last week's. Make one chart and a five line summary of what changed, and draft it in a canvas I can send to my team.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Read the plan Work mode shows you before you approve it. It is the cheapest place to catch a wrong file, a wrong inbox or a step you did not ask for.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Features worth knowing","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Mistral's capabilities overview lists Think mode, which uses its reasoning model for harder questions; Voice mode, so you can talk instead of type; Deep Research for multi-step web research; a Code Interpreter that runs Python in a secure environment; Canvas, an editor you work in together with the assistant; and image generation with models from Black Forest Labs. The help center adds that web search can draw on news from AFP and AP.","sources":[{"name":"Mistral help center: What is Le Chat and how do I use it","url":"https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347453-what-is-le-chat-and-how-do-i-use-it"},{"name":"Mistral help center: An overview of Le Chat's capabilities","url":"https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347531-an-overview-of-le-chat-s-capabilities"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Work mode also has Skills, reusable workflows that Mistral says are built on open standards. In heise's test, skills could be turned on or off one by one, loaded automatically or called by naming them in a prompt, and users could import their own skills written in Markdown. A pre-installed skill-creator helps you build new ones.","sources":[{"name":"Mistral AI: Vibe announcement","url":"https://mistral.ai/it/news/vibe-agent/"},{"name":"heise: Mistral Vibe, trying out the Work and Code interfaces","url":"https://heise.de/-11312502"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Plans and what the free version leaves out","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Mistral's announcement lists four plans: Free for quick answers and simple everyday tasks, Pro at $14.99 a month, Team at $24.99 per user a month with a shared workspace and admin controls, and Enterprise with custom deployments. The help center says the free plan includes most features with daily caps, Pro removes the cap on messages, and a discounted Pro plan exists for eligible students and educators.","sources":[{"name":"Mistral help center: What is Le Chat and how do I use it","url":"https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347453-what-is-le-chat-and-how-do-i-use-it"},{"name":"Mistral AI: Vibe announcement","url":"https://mistral.ai/it/news/vibe-agent/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Exact limits are hard to pin down. heise reported that the free plan cannot create canvases or run remote coding sessions, and that Pro and Team get five times as many web searches and up to 40 times as many image generations as Free, but that Mistral does not publish the underlying numbers. The Decoder also noted that Mistral had not given concrete usage limits for Work mode. heise quoted prices in euros that differ from the dollar prices on Mistral's page, so check the price shown in your own account.","sources":[{"name":"heise: Mistral Vibe, trying out the Work and Code interfaces","url":"https://heise.de/-11312502"},{"name":"The Decoder: Mistral rebrands Le Chat as Vibe","url":"https://the-decoder.com/mistral-rebrands-lechat-as-vibe-betting-its-chatbots-future-is-as-a-full-blown-work-agent/"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"On the free plan, the help center says your conversations may be used to train Mistral's models unless you opt out in your account settings. Do that before you paste in anything private.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where it falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The rename makes Vibe harder to learn than Le Chat was. There are now three modes, one of them due to be retired, and the help pages are split between the old help center and Mistral's developer docs. heise also found rough edges in Work mode: a writing skill could not pull information from connected apps on its own, and pre-installed skills could not be changed with the skill-creator.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The practical approach is to start in Chat with one real question you would otherwise search for, then try Work mode on one small, repeatable job, such as a weekly summary from a single spreadsheet. If the plan it writes matches what you would have done yourself, give it a bigger task. If it keeps hitting the free caps, that is the point to decide whether Pro is worth it for you.","sources":[]}]}

item.author: NeuraFeed news desk

item.title: How to use Photoroom for product photos
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Upload a photo in the app or at app.photoroom.com. The background is removed automatically. Shoot on a plain surface in good light for the cleanest edge. Pick a plain white background for marketplaces, or let AI Backgrounds build a styled scene. Add an AI shadow so the product does not look pasted on. Batch mode applies the same edits to many photos at once. Free accounts get 250 exports a month. Paid plans start at $7.50 a month, billed yearly. Sources: Photoroom: Pricing, Photoroom: Batch mode, Photoroom: Background remover, eesel AI: Photoroom pricing guide.

On the pricing page, with yearly billing, Pro costs $7.50 a month with 8,000 AI credits and 1,000 exports, Max costs $20.99 a month with 25,000 AI credits and 3,000 exports, and Ultra costs $82.50 a month with 75,000 AI credits and 10,000 exports. Choose a background","text":"For marketplaces that want a plain look, use a white background. The Research Agent answers a question in plain language and can reach beyond papers, to the web, trial registries and files you upload. A Research Report searches, screens and extracts automatically and writes a structured answer, with templates such as General Review, 1-Page Overview and Research Gap Analysis. The Systematic Review is the step by step workflow where you control every stage. The older Find Papers, Extract Data and Chat with Papers tools were replaced by the Research Agent.","sources":[{"name":"Elicit Help Center: Elicit's Research Agent","url":"https://support.elicit.com/en/articles/14756886-elicit-s-research-agent"},{"name":"Elicit Help Center: Research Reports","url":"https://support.elicit.com/en/articles/14756862-get-a-research-report-to-generate-in-depth-answers-automatically-in-elicit"},{"name":"Elicit Help Center: Export your data","url":"https://support.elicit.com/en/articles/14758189-export-your-data-from-elicit"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use a Research Report when you need a fast map of a topic or a list of seed papers. Use the Systematic Review when you need to show your method, such as screening criteria and reasons for each exclusion, to a supervisor or a journal.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to run a literature review in Elicit","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Write a short, focused question","text":"On the setup page, Elicit asks for your research question. Its help center recommends two or three sentences at most. Additional context: Include randomized controlled trials and cohort studies published since [year]. Exclude studies in [group you want to leave out]. I care most about [main outcome] and [secondary outcome].","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose the stages and the search type","text":"Gather, Extraction and Report are always on. Screen abstracts, then full texts","text":"Elicit writes screening criteria from your question. You can edit, switch off or add criteria before you click Run screening. Extract data into columns","text":"Add columns for what you want from each paper, such as sample size, study design or main result. The help center suggests plain English column names and testing a few columns on a small set first. Then click Run extraction. Study design (RCT, cohort, case control, other)
Population (age, country, setting)
Main outcome and how it was measured
Main result (effect size with confidence interval if reported)
Limitations the authors mention","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Generate the report and export","text":"The Report step writes up the highest scoring papers: 80 by default, up to 135 on Pro and up to 200 on Scale and Enterprise. Reports download as PDF or Word. Plus adds table exports and more extraction columns. The Systematic Review workflow starts at Pro, which Elicit lists at $49 a month on monthly billing, with lower prices on yearly billing. Scale adds live collaboration and extraction from figures, and dual human review is only on Enterprise.","sources":[{"name":"Elicit Help Center: Systematic reviews in Elicit","url":"https://support.elicit.com/en/articles/14759154-systematic-reviews-in-elicit"},{"name":"Elicit pricing","url":"https://elicit.com/pricing"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Elicit falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Elicit's own help center says gray literature and some trial reports are harder to find, and that some regional publications, including some Chinese journals, are missing, so it suggests adding specialized databases. A University of British Columbia library wiki cites a 2026 study in Research Synthesis Methods that found Elicit's data extraction can complement human extractors but not replace them, and the librarians recommend it for early stage searching and finding seed papers rather than as the only search for a systematic review.","sources":[{"name":"Elicit Help Center: Elicit's source for papers","url":"https://support.elicit.com/en/articles/14758040-elicit-s-source-for-papers"},{"name":"UBC Wiki: Elicit.com","url":"https://wiki.ubc.ca/Elicit.com"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"In practice, the time saving is real for the first pass: finding papers you missed, drafting criteria and filling a first version of a data table. Check every extracted number you plan to report, keep your own record of why papers were excluded, and run the same search in at least one database your field expects, such as PubMed or Scopus.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Before you run extraction on hundreds of papers, run it on ten you already know well. If Elicit gets those wrong, rename the column more precisely and try again. It uses less of your monthly allowance than fixing a full table later.","sources":[]}]}

OpenAI notes that the last screenshot can sometimes come back blank even when the task finished.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Schedule it if it repeats","text":"Scheduled tasks can run once, on a schedule, or when something changes. Use them for things like a weekly summary of a shared folder or a daily check of a price or a status page.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts to copy","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Book-ready restaurant options","text":"Find three restaurants near [neighborhood] that have a table for [number] people on [day] at [time]. Keep it under [budget] per person and skip anything with fewer than 4 stars. Do not book anything. Give me the name, the open time slot and the link for each.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Track a package from your email","text":"Look in my connected email for the shipping confirmation from [store]. Open the carrier's public tracking page and tell me where the package is and when it should arrive. If tracking needs a sign-in, stop and tell me.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Turn files into a deck","text":"Use the files in @Google Drive folder [folder name] and the last two weeks of messages in @Slack channel [channel]. Make a 6-slide summary for [audience]: the goal, progress, numbers, risks and next steps. List the file each number came from.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A weekly check-in","text":"Every Monday at 8 a.m., check [page or folder] for changes since last week and send me a five-line summary. If nothing changed, say so in one line.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What it still cannot do","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The cloud browser cannot sign in to sites, take passwords, use autofill or password managers, or complete payments at launch, and a task that needs any of these stops. CAPTCHAs and sites that block automated access can also stop it, and some sites are blocked for safety or compliance reasons, so you may need to finish the last step yourself. On iPhone, a task can look stuck after you approve an action; reopening the conversation or continuing on the web fixes it.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: Using cloud browser in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/20001280-using-cloud-browser-in-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Usage follows the same model as Codex: there is no fixed message count, and complex tasks use more of your plan's allowance than simple ones. That is a change from agent mode's flat 40 or 400 messages a month.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: ChatGPT for your most ambitious work","url":"https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-for-your-most-ambitious-work/"},{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: ChatGPT agent","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/11752874-chatgpt-agent"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Never paste passwords or card numbers into the chat. If a connected app can do the job directly, OpenAI recommends using the app instead of the browser, and it suggests stopping a task the moment it opens the wrong site.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Work also reads far more of your data than a normal chat does, which VentureBeat flagged as a privacy trade-off. You can remove saved browser data from the cloud browser in ChatGPT settings.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/openai-introduces-chatgpt-work-a-cloud-based-ai-agent-that-manages-tasks-across-email-slack-and-calendars"},{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: Using cloud browser in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/20001280-using-cloud-browser-in-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Agent mode was a single tool you switched on for one task. Work is closer to a place you hand projects to: it keeps context across steps, connects to the apps you already use and can repeat a job on a schedule. The catch is that it still stops at sign-ins and payments, so the most useful tasks today are research, comparisons, drafts and files you review before anything goes out.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Freepik AI, now called Magnific, for images and video
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open the Image Generator, write a prompt, choose a style, aspect ratio and model, or leave it on Auto. Then click Generate. Under References, click + Add to steer the result with a character, an object, a style or a color palette. You can combine several. Sources: Magnific: Freepik is now Magnific, Magnific docs: Your first AI image, Magnific docs: Video Generator, Magnific docs: AI credits and limits, Magnific docs: AI content and copyright, Magnific pricing, The Next Web, Tech.eu, Vmake review, Magnific docs: Plans and pricing.

Here is how its image and video generators work, what the free plan gives you and when you need to pay.","summary":"Freepik relaunched as Magnific in April 2026, and its AI suite runs more than 30 image models and video models such as Veo, Kling and Sora 2 from one place. Free accounts get up to 20 images a day for personal use.","tags":["Freepik","Magnific","AI image generator","AI video","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Freepik's AI tools now live under a new name. The company relaunched as Magnific on April 28, 2026, and freepik.com now sends you to magnific.com. Your login, plan and existing licenses did not change, according to the company. If you want to know how to use Freepik AI, it is the same suite: an image generator, a video generator, an upscaler and editing tools in one place, alongside a stock library of more than 250 million assets.","sources":[{"name":"Magnific: Freepik is now Magnific","url":"https://www.magnific.com/ai/docs/freepik-is-now-magnific"},{"name":"The Next Web","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/freepik-rebrands-as-magnific"},{"name":"Tech.eu","url":"https://tech.eu/2026/04/28/freepik-rebrands-as-magnific-unifying-its-ai-creative-stack-as-enterprise-and-no-collar-growth-accelerates/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The selling point is not a model of its own. Magnific mostly gives you other companies' models, such as Google's Nano Banana and Veo, Kling, Seedream, Flux and OpenAI's GPT Image and Sora, behind one prompt box and one credit balance. This guide covers the image generator, the video generator, what the free plan really gives you, and what you may do with the results.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use the Freepik (Magnific) AI image generator","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Sign in and open the AI Suite","text":"Create an account or click Sign in, then open the AI Suite from the top menu. The Image Generator is one of the tools listed there.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Write a prompt","text":"Type what you want to see in the prompt field. The optional AI prompt feature can rewrite a short idea into a more detailed prompt. If you have a picture but no words, Upload image to describe writes a prompt from the image for you.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Choose a style, aspect ratio and model","text":"Pick a style and an aspect ratio, then a model. The help center says there are more than 30 models, including Nano Banana, Seedream, Flux, GPT Image 2, Ideogram, Recraft and Mystic. If you do not want to choose, set the model to Auto. You can make 1 to 4 images per prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Auto for your first tries. Once you like a result, note which model made it and pick that model directly. Quality varies noticeably between models, so the same prompt can look very different from one to the next.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Add references when you need control","text":"Under References, click + Add to attach a Character, an Object, a Style, a Color palette, a Camera setting or an Effect. You can combine them. To start from your own picture instead, click Upload in the prompt field, then Use image.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Click Generate and find your results","text":"Click Generate. Finished images appear under Recent creations and stay in the History tab, so you can come back to them later and keep editing on the same page.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you need the same person in many images, Magnific lets you train a custom character from photos and call it with a short tag such as @jane. Training takes 10 to 30 minutes, per the help center. Only use photos of people who have agreed to it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A clean product shot","text":"A [product] on a plain [color] background, soft studio light from the left, shot from slightly above, sharp focus, lots of empty space on the right for text","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A social media header","text":"Wide banner image for a [topic] blog: [main subject] in the center, calm colors, simple shapes, no text, plenty of space at the top","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use the Freepik (Magnific) AI video generator","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Write the prompt and pick a model","text":"Type a prompt, then choose the model, aspect ratio and duration. Enhance prompt with AI and the Prompt Editor are optional helpers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Animate an image, or set the ending","text":"To animate a picture, use the Image tab. Turn on End image when you want to decide what the last frame looks like. Multi-shot lets you build up to 6 shots, and some models can add sound effects.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Click Generate video","text":"Click Generate video. Clips are typically 4 to 15 seconds long, so plan longer pieces as several shots and join them in an editor.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Bring a photo to life","text":"Slow push in toward [subject]. Light wind moves [hair, leaves, fabric]. Camera stays steady, natural light, no sudden cuts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Freepik AI free plan, credits and prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan gives you up to 20 AI images per day using the in-house model, according to the help center. It has no credit balance, and you cannot buy extra credits on it. The documentation does not list a free allowance for video.","sources":[{"name":"Magnific docs: AI credits and limits","url":"https://www.magnific.com/no/ai/docs/ai-credits-and-limits"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Paid plans run on credits, and each tool costs a different number of credits. The pricing page lists Premium at $20 a month, Plus at $45 and Pro at $110 when billed monthly, with lower prices for annual billing. Plus and higher plans include Relax mode, which the company says gives free generations on most image models, while most video models and the upscaler still use credits. The help center notes that credit costs can change.","sources":[{"name":"Magnific pricing","url":"https://www.magnific.com/pricing?p=new"},{"name":"Magnific docs: Plans and pricing","url":"https://www.magnific.com/ai/docs/plans-and-pricing"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Using Freepik AI images commercially","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Commercial use needs a paid plan. The help center says AI-generated images and videos may be used commercially, that paid plans include a commercial license, and that free plans are limited to personal use with attribution. It also warns that the company cannot guarantee copyright ownership of AI output in every country, and that you are responsible for making sure your results do not copy someone else's work or show real people without their consent.","sources":[{"name":"Magnific docs: AI content and copyright","url":"https://www.magnific.com/ai/docs/ai-content-and-copyright"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Freepik AI is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"An independent review from Vmake found that image quality varies a lot between models, that complex prompts often need several attempts, that credits get expensive for heavy users and that the strongest models sit on higher tiers. The Next Web noted that Magnific uses the same frontier models as its rivals, so its edge is the workflow rather than the models.","sources":[{"name":"The Next Web","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/freepik-rebrands-as-magnific"},{"name":"Vmake review","url":"https://vmake.ai/blog/freepik-ai-image-generator-review"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you only ever use one model, the company that makes it may sell it to you more cheaply on its own site. Magnific makes most sense when you switch between many image and video models in one project.","sources":[]}]}
